title: Del Valle Land Annexation Hearing in Austin
summary:
*   A public hearing was held to discuss the full annexation of approximately 1,120 acres in the Del Valle area.
*   This proposed expansion aimed to bring land situated east of U.S. 183 and south of SH 71 under full city jurisdiction.
*   Various city departments, including police, fire, water, and health services, presented plans for providing services to the annexed territory.
*   The public hearing regarding the Del Valle annexation was formally concluded.
transcript:
Austin City Council
MINUTES
SPECIAL CALLED MEETING
MONDAY, AUGUST 6, 2001
The City Council of Austin, Texas, convened in a regular meeting on August 6, 2001 at the
South Rural Health Center, 3518 FM 973 South, Austin, Texas.
Mayor Watson called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.
1. 
Conduct a Public Hearing on the full purpose annexation of the Del Valle area
(approximately, 1120 acres extending on the east side of U.S. 183, from the existing full
purpose city limits near Hergotz Lane southeastwards along U.S. 183 and north of SH 71,
to the existing full purpose city limits at Falwell Lane.
The presentation was made by Ben Luckens, Planning, Transportation and
Sustainabilty; Commander Brad 
Conner, Austin Police Department; 
Pieter
Sybersma, Austin Fire Department; Richard Harrington, Director, Emergency
Medical Services; Mike Boyle, Water and Wastewater; Ed Poppitt, Street and Bridge;
Alan Hughes, Public Works and Transportation; Jose Guerrera, Watershed
Protection; Gregory Bolds, Health and Human Services; and Ann Hargrove, Solid
Waste Services.
The public hearing was closed on Council Member Slusher's motion, Council
Member Griffith's second by a 4-0 vote. Council Members Alvarez, Thomas and
Wynn were absent.
The motion to adjourn the meeting at 7:25 p.m. was approved on Council Member
Slusher's motion, Council Member Griffith's second by a 4-0 vote. 
Council Members
Alvarez, Thomas and Wynn were absent.
The amended minutes for the regular meeting of July 19, 2001, Special Called
Meetings of August 2, August 6, and August 9, 2001 and the minutes for regular
meeting of August 9, 2001 were approved.
